title: Envoy Proxy Architecture Deep Dive
description: Investigation of Envoy's threading model, xDS protocol, and operational trade-offs relative to managed API Gateway offerings.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Envoy is a cloud-native L7 proxy written in C++. Each worker thread handles a subset of connections; the main thread owns the xDS subscription loop and fans updates out without locking hot paths.

sections.heading: xDS Control Plane Protocol
sections.body: Envoy discovers routes, clusters, listeners, and endpoints via streaming gRPC (xDS v3). The control plane pushes a DiscoveryResponse; Envoy applies it atomically and ACKs. Stale configs are never visible during an update.

sections.heading: Threading Model
sections.body: One listener thread accepts connections and dispatches to `N` worker threads (configurable via `--concurrency`). Each worker thread runs a libevent loop. Upstream connection pools are per-thread, eliminating cross-thread lock contention.

sections.heading: Observability
sections.body: Envoy exposes a Prometheus-compatible `/stats/prometheus` endpoint and supports distributed tracing via Zipkin, Jaeger, or OpenTelemetry. Access logs are structured JSON by default.

sections.heading: Verdict
sections.body: Envoy is a strong fit: sub-millisecond overhead in benchmarks, mature xDS ecosystem, and first-class Kubernetes integration via Istio or Gateway API. Main cost is operational complexity of the control plane.
